Entropy-Based Gravity Model

Source: R/centrality-batch68.R
centrality_entropy_gravity.Rd

The entropy-based gravity model (Yan et al. 2020) combines the node H-index, closeness, betweenness and PageRank of a node into one mass with entropy weights, and adds the gravity between the node and the nodes within \(r\) steps: $$G(i) = \sum_{j:\, 1 \le d_{ij} \le r} \frac{C_i C_j}{d_{ij}^2}, \qquad C_i = \sum_{k=1}^{4} w_k b_{ik}, \qquad w_k = \frac{1 - S_k}{4 - \sum_l S_l},$$ with \(d_{ij}\) the distance, \(b_{ik}\) the \(k\)-th attribute of node \(i\) min-max scaled over the nodes, and \(S_k\) the entropy of the shares \(b_{ik} / \sum_i b_{ik}\) divided by \(\ln N\).

Usage

centrality_entropy_gravity(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses entropy_gravity_radius (default 3) and damping (the PageRank damping factor, default 0.85).

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. The source prints its equation (3) with the shares taken over the attributes of one node and its equation (5) with the entropies \(S_k\) in place of the weights \(w_k\). Its text describes the entropy of each attribute across the nodes, a lower entropy giving a larger weight, and a combination by weighted averaging, which is what is computed (owner decision 2026-11-26); read literally, equation (3) gives a negative weight on the kite network. As in the source's equation (3), an attribute at which only one node is above the minimum takes the shares \((1 + b_{ik}) / \sum_i (1 + b_{ik})\) instead. The attributes are those of the source's chosen combination: the node H-index (centrality_lobby), closeness as the reciprocal of the sum of distances, betweenness, and PageRank (centrality_pagerank) with damping, which at damping = 1 is the degree share, the stationary distribution of the random walk; min-max scaling removes their scale. entropy_gravity_radius is \(r\), 3 by default as in the source (the Centrality Zoo says 2); Inf admits every node. Scaled values within \(10^{-9}\) of 0 count as the minimum, so that nodes equal in exact arithmetic are not separated by rounding. An attribute with the same value at every node, as on any regular network, makes the min-max scaling 0/0; the measure then warns (class cograph_undefined_measure) and returns NA. It does the same on a disconnected or a one-node network, where closeness has no value. The source prints no value, so the implementation is checked against the definition only. On four test networks the score ranks nodes closest to multi_evidence and hybrid (mean Kendall correlation 0.90); with closeness the correlation is 0.77 to 0.92. A entropy_gravity_radius that is not a whole number of at least one or Inf raises a cograph_bad_parameter error. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Yan, X.-L., Cui, Y.-P. and Ni, S.-J. (2020). Identifying influential spreaders in complex networks based on entropy weight method and gravity law. Chinese Physics B, 29(4), 048902. doi:10.1088/1674-1056/ab77fe .

See also

centrality_gravity, centrality_egm, centrality_lobby, centrality_pagerank, centrality.

Examples

centrality_entropy_gravity(to_undirected(regulation_net))
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>   1.597388   2.619912   3.699044   2.729238   1.029741   1.728506   0.000000 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>   1.741642   2.692761   1.730051 
centrality_entropy_gravity(to_undirected(regulation_net), entropy_gravity_radius = 2)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>   1.597388   2.619912   3.699044   2.729238   1.029741   1.728506   0.000000 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>   1.741642   2.692761   1.730051
